A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PYRREGULAR and retain the same central framework and classification benchmark. Their complete main texts, appendices, rotated tables, figures, and embedded notebooks support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and runtime experiments involving 12 models and 34 datasets, plus fine-tuning experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds framework resource measurements, regression results, and analyses of model performance.

M1.justification: The COO/xarray representation and dense timestamp-ranking conversion remain unchanged. v2 adds a limited downstream regression adaptation by replacing classification heads with regression heads (Appendix F); Appendix G demonstrates BORF followed by LassoCV.

E1.justification: The 34 classification datasets and their tasks are retained. Appendix F adds a pilot regression evaluation on four existing datasets: age prediction on MI3 and P19, SAPS-I prediction on P12, and productivity prediction on PGE. Forecasting and anomaly detection remain proposed extensions.

E2.justification: The classification comparator sets, including Table 3's fine-tuned comparison, are unchanged. The regression pilot introduces a NAIVE mean-target baseline alongside regression variants of BORF, LGBM, and ROCKET. Table 4 newly compares the proposed representation against raw storage and two dense representations.

E3.justification: Existing classification splits, hyperparameters, computational budgets, and metrics are retained. New protocols include untuned regression evaluated with RMSE, a tutorial using MAPE, and resource profiling of datasets exceeding 10 MB using loading/conversion time, disk usage, and memory consumption.

E4.justification: v2 adds framework scalability profiling in Section 5.2, model rank-correlation clustering in Figure 20, and worst-dataset/worst-to-average-rank analysis in Table 7. These examine computational costs, complementary model behavior, and failures hidden by average rankings. The existing subgroup plots and multiple-comparison matrices are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three-run averaging for the same stochastic models, the existing uncertainty entries, and Holm-corrected Wilcoxon testing at 0.05. The added descriptive analyses introduce no additional repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Table 3 and the complete classification F1/runtime tables are unchanged after matching renumbered tables. Substantial new results include resource measurements, regression scores, correlations, and worst-case ratios. For example, Table 4 reports TA memory of 0.34 GB for sparse storage versus 4135.02 GB for fully ragged dense storage; Table 11 reports P12 RMSE of 4.11 for LGBM versus 5.97 for NAIVE. These are new evaluations, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: New Appendix B supplements the existing taxonomy with formal definitions and explicit counterexample arguments establishing pairwise non-implication among irregularity types. Section 5.2 also adds sorting-cost and sparse-versus-dense memory-complexity reasoning. The original representation equations are retained.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the irregularity taxonomy, interoperable representation, standardized classification repository, and 34-dataset/12-model benchmark. The main conclusion about strong generalist performance and task-specific advantages from specialist tuning is retained; the new evidence supplements these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds substantive interpretations of model correlations, dataset-specific failures, and why strong average rankings do not guarantee robustness. It also discusses limitations of explainers handling irregular inputs. Appendix F specifies possible task extensions while explicitly qualifying regression results as preliminary and their targets as insufficiently curated.

D1.justification: v2 adds regression and PyTorch usage examples, including concrete regression pipelines, while retaining existing model hyperparameters and hardware information. It removes the direct dataset-hosting URL, replacing its experimental-details footnote with a redaction notice, and changes the documentation pointer. Loading instructions and the code-repository link remain.

R1.justification: v2 extends discussion to missing-value explainability and prospective graph, state-space, LLM, and multimodal methods, including Time-LLM and CALF. It also removes several citations, including SHAP and Pooch. These are bounded extensions to positioning; the central relationship to existing time-series libraries and benchmarks remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction and several explanatory passages are tightened, terminology increasingly uses ITS, and TIMESNET's description is corrected from transformer-based to inception-based. New sections organize the added material, while most existing exposition and its sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the resource, worst-case, and regression tables and the correlation heatmap, and adds a PyTorch icon to Figure 3. It changes title/header styling, citation presentation, and notebook pagination. Existing benchmark plots and tables are largely retained, with relocation and renumbering rather than redesign.

improvement.justification: Section 5.2 supplies useful quantitative support for the framework's efficiency claims, while the formal counterexamples and failure analyses improve justification and interpretation. These strengthen an otherwise retained classification study. The regression pilot is appropriately qualified, but its provisional targets and the removal of the direct dataset link limit the overall gain.
